messages:
mira: ran an nsys capture against the prod-like replay; saw matmul workspace spikes and repeated cudaMallocAsync churn after the adaptive kernel-selector landed. attaching perfetto/trace link: https://perfetto.link/abcd1234 :eyes:

sam: which change exactly? the probe heuristic or the fallback path?

mira: probe heuristic (adaptive-kernel-select @runtime). it picks split-K for lots of shapes now. timeline shows split-K attempts, workspace allocs, then immediate free, then another alloc a few ms later. pattern repeats during midbatch.

jonah: that smells like workspace sizing oscillation. do we have nvtx markers around kernel selection?

mira: yes — added NVTX around selection and cublasLt calls. snippet from nsys timeline (transcribed):
```
NVTX: choose_algo(shape=1024x64) -> splitK(algo=2, ws=5.2MB)
cudaMallocAsync(5.2MB) @0x7f...
cuBLASLtMatmul(algo=splitK)
cudaFreeAsync(5.2MB)
...
NVTX: choose_algo(shape=1024x64) -> default(algo=0, ws=2.1MB)
cudaMallocAsync(2.1MB)
cuBLASLtMatmul(algo=default)
```

eli: do we observe increased latency or more out-of-memory?

mira: p90 latency +18%, p99 +60% on that workload; no OOM but mempool fragmentation and midbatch eviction events (kv-cache logs show evict keys during that window).

dena: is the KV cache eviction correlated with the workspace alloc bursts?

mira: yes. perf trace timestamps line up: when workspace allocs spike, we see KV cache evict cycles immediately after. hypothesis: frequent varying workspace sizes cause allocator to fall back to cudaMallocAsync instead of reusing pool slab -> mempool pressure -> midbatch kv eviction.

sam: can you paste the allocator debug log around a spike?

mira: pasted excerpt: 
```
[allocator] slab_request(size=5242880) -> no_free_slab, fallback async_alloc
[allocator] async_alloc 5242880 -> success (ptr=0x7fabc)
[allocator] free 5242880 -> returned to cuda (no slab reclaim)
[kvcache] midbatch_evict(reason=mempool_pressure, keys=42)
```

jonah: interesting. so split-K sometimes needs larger workspace and we don't reserve enough headroom in slab buckets. solution paths: 1) adjust slab quantization to include that size class; 2) prefer kernel variants with smaller workspace for lat-sensitive routes; 3) warmup probe to allocate and pin largest observed workspace earlier so it comes from slabs.

eli: option 3 might help latency but increases steady resident memory. tradeoff depends on SLA.

mira: I ran a quick A/B: pin to smaller-workspace variant => p99 back to normal but throughput down ~4%. warmup approach => p99 stable, memory +6% resident.

perf-bot: perf/regression-checker found +14% p99 regression on branch runtime/adaptive-kernel-select vs baseline (2026-03-15). details: https://perf.ci/reports/1765439999

dena: good to have CI repro. next steps?

sam: short term: revert heuristic for PL1 routes or add route-level policy to prefer low-ws kernels. medium: change allocator to map large workspace sizes into existing slab bins (coalescing) and add warmup for probe choices. long: improve kernel selector cost model to include mempool pressure cost.

mira: I'll open an RFC with timeline and add reproducer script (replay + nsys capture). filing issue with logs + perf trace.

jonah: can you also include perfetto flamegraph and the slice showing cudaMallocAsync hotspots? that helps infra folks.

mira: will do. adding checklist: 
- [ ] issue + repro script (mira)
- [ ] short-term route policy to avoid big-ws kernels on latency tier (sam)
- [ ] allocator bucket tweak experiment (eli)
- [ ] update kernel selector cost model (jonah)
- [ ] perftrace + flamegraph uploaded (mira)

sam: thanks — let's sync in 30 with a quick triage. :thumbsup:
